land.text: the Matan lands round Sukadana and the Kayong and Kendawangan rivers

successors.note: The page: 'Panembahan Anom was dismissed as sultan in 1833'; the Matan line went on as a Dutch-controlled Panembahan (1833-1835 Prince Cakra Negara; from 1835 'Due to Dutch intervention' Prince Anom again, to 1847; a Gubernemen decree of 11 March 1847; the territories joined the Wester-afdeeling by a decree of 27 August 1849). The infobox says 'Part of the Dutch East Indies (from 1779)'. After Gusti Asma (1762-1819) the centre moved to Simpang and the Kayong-Matan (Second Tanjungpura) kingdom split off.

capitals.name: Sukadana
capitals.note: Infobox 'Sukadana (1590)': the move followed Panembahan Sorgi (Giri Kesuma) embracing Islam. Coordinates are the modern town of Sukadana (the page gives none).

capitals.name: Matan (Indra Laya / Sungai Matan, near Ketapang)
capitals.note: 'The centre of government moved again in 1637 to the Indra Laya region'; 'During the reign of Sultan Muhammad Zainuddin (1665-1724), the centre of the palace shifted again' (Sungai Matan); later moves to Kartapura, Tanjungpura village and Muliakerta are undated on the page. The page's two dates conflict; the position is the Ketapang area, approximate.

correction.text: the Cliopatria outline, begun 29 years early: Sukadana is the capital from 1590 under Panembahan Sorgi (Giri Kesuma, 1590-1604)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins in 1619; the infobox gives Sukadana as capital in 1590 and the ruler list opens Gusti Aliuddin (Giri Kesuma, Panembahan Sorgi) 1590-1604. The page describes the old Tanjungpura territory as running from Tanjung Dato to Tanjung Sambar, a longer coast than this outline.

11.5 k km2 on the Kayong, Matan and Kendawangan coast (lat -3.06 to -0.94). The page gives no area. It describes territory running from Tanjung Dato to Tanjung Sambar, which the Cliopatria rows of Sambas, Mempawah, Pontianak (from 1772) and Sukadana together cover only in part; the outline is the southern, Matan half.
Same outline as 1619-1829, to 1833: Panembahan Anom was 'dismissed as sultan in 1833'. Nothing on the page changes the land in 1830.

region.text: Sukadana and the Matan coast, the seat from 1590

ledger.note: 1590: Sukadana becomes the seat of the Tanjungpura kingdom. The infobox lists 'Sukadana (1590)' as the capital after Panembahan Sorgi (Giri Kesuma) embraced Islam; the page calls Tanjungpura 'an eighth century Malay kingdom' (infobox 'Established: 8th Century'), so 1590 starts the Sukadana state, not the kingdom.
1622: Giri Mustaka becomes the first Sultan. 'Giri Mustaka (1622-1665)' is 'the first king of the Tanjungpura Kingdom with the title Sultan'. Same state and land: colour continues.
1637: 'The centre of government moved again in 1637 to the Indra Laya region' (the page also dates a later move to Sungai Matan under Sultan Muhammad Zainuddin, 1665-1724).

region.text: the Matan lands, from 1833 under Dutch-appointed Panembahan

ledger.note: 1833: Panembahan Anom is dismissed and the Matan line passes under Dutch influence. 'Panembahan Anom was dismissed as sultan in 1833 because he was considered disloyal to Sultan Abdul Jalil'; 'Due to Dutch intervention, starting in 1835 Prince Anom was again seated as Panembahan Matan until 1847'. The year is Cliopatria's last; the page's reading of it as the end of the sultanate is mine.

wars.name: Dutch war on Sukadana
wars.outcome: 'The Dutch came to Sukadana in 1604 and fought a war with Queen Sukadana until the queen was replaced.'
wars.note: No land changed hands; the page gives no end year for the war.

wars.name: Mataram expedition against Matan
wars.outcome: 'Adipati Kendal with his Mataram Expedition, attacked Matan (1622)'; the Mataram page has Sultan Agung 'capturing Sukadana, Surabaya's ally in southwest Kalimantan in 1622'. This page records no vassalage and no release.
wars.note: The mataram-sultanate dossier carries the vassal_start (confidence 1 for the end).

certainty.note: The page describes the realm by capes (Tanjung Dato to Tanjung Sambar) and rivers, not by a boundary; the outline is Cliopatria's.

sources.title: Tanjungpura Kingdom

notes: One page was opened (twice, with two questions; budget 1-2). The Wikipedia article is the Tanjungpura Kingdom, an '8th century' kingdom with capitals Negeri Baru (1487), Sukadana (1590), Sungai Matan and later seats; Cliopatria's row is its Sukadana/Matan phase (1619-1833). The dossier starts at 1590, the page's Sukadana date, and ends at 1833, Cliopatria's year, which fits the page's dismissal of Panembahan Anom; the Matan line lasted until at least the 1847 Gubernemen decree and the page's infobox says 'Part of the Dutch East Indies (from 1779)', a date no sentence explains. The page's ruler lists conflict (Gusti Asma 1762-1819 against 1792-1830; Zainuddin 1665-1724 against 1659-1725), so no ruler strip was written. The 'Sultanate of Sukadana' name is the Hikayat Banjar's, not an article's. Mempawah, Landak and Pontianak are not described as vassals on this page (a Landak princess was Giri Kesuma's wife; Mempawah's descendants live there); the Mempawah page ties Mempawah to Matan before 1740 without saying how. The Mataram page lists Sukadana among Mataram's vassals (see the mataram-sultanate dossier). Capital coordinates are approximate, and Sukadana, Matan and Ketapang are not in the gazetteer.
